hypothesis: At N=256 the trained-force-R2 shortfall relative to N=128 is slower growth, not a lower ceiling. Seeds 24-25 (data_seed 0, 4 layers, d_model=64, e in [0, 0.5], m2 in [0.1, 1], best-of-3 controls) were 0.054-0.076 below their N=128 3000-step trained force R2 (0.639 / 0.621) at 3000 steps. Trained to 4000 steps, they close most of that gap. All values come from run-record probes_final (best-margin layer, unrounded). Within-run growth is measured from the step-3000 checkpoint to step 4000, also from the run records. Because the lr schedule may depend on total steps, cross-run comparisons are reported as horizon-confounded if the step-3000 trained force R2 differs by more than 0.03 from the 3000-step runs of the same seeds (0.563 / 0.559).
expected_if_true: In both seeds, final best-layer trained force R2 at step 4000 is within 0.02 of the same seed's N=128 value (>= 0.619 for seed 24, >= 0.601 for seed 25), and it rises by >= 0.03 between steps 3000 and 4000. The force control R2 is unchanged because the controls are fixed per run. The headroom-normalised accel_step margin stays in [0.60, 0.78].
expected_if_false: In both seeds, final trained force R2 stays >= 0.04 below the same seed's N=128 value (<= 0.599 for seed 24, <= 0.581 for seed 25) and gains <= 0.015 between steps 3000 and 4000. That would mean N=256 has a lower force-decodability ceiling, not just a later one. Any mixed result is reported as inconclusive.
